name: reverseport

tools.name: re_scan
tools.description: Reconnaissance of a folder: detects the engine/framework (Godot, Unity, Unreal, GameMaker, RPG Maker, Ren'Py, LÖVE, Defold, Bevy, MonoGame, three.js/Phaser/Electron, Flutter, .NET, Go, Rust, Python…) for source projects AND exported game builds, languages with line counts, file categories, entry points, biggest files and binaries. Start here.

tools.name: re_graph
tools.description: Builds the dependency graph of a project: imports/includes/requires, Godot res:// loads and scene resources, Unity script/prefab GUIDs, and type references (C#, GDScript class_name/autoloads, Java…). Returns entry points, cycles, orphans, most-used files, external packages and the port order (dependencies first). format:"mermaid" adds a diagram.

limit.description: Files in portOrder (default 80; edges 40). Larger values return more.

tools.name: re_symbols
tools.description: Code structure for one file or a whole folder (30+ languages: GDScript, C#, C/C++ incl. Unreal macros, Python, JS/TS, Lua, Java/Kotlin, Go, Rust, Swift, shaders, Ren'Py…): classes with base classes, functions with lines, signals/events, exported/serialized fields, dependencies, node paths. match filters by name (substring or * wildcard).

tools.name: re_scene
tools.description: Reads Godot .tscn/.tres/project.godot (Godot 3 and 4) and Unity .unity/.prefab/.asset (text serialization) into one neutral tree: node names, types, scripts, transforms (position, quaternion, scale), components, groups/tags, instanced scenes/prefabs (resolved through .meta GUIDs), signal connections, plus a mermaid diagram.

tools.name: re_binary
tools.description: Inspects PE/EXE/DLL (incl. .NET assemblies: runtime, types and methods), ELF, Mach-O (incl. universal), WebAssembly, Java .class, Android .dex, Lua/LuaJIT and Python bytecode: architecture, sections with entropy, imports/exports, PDB path, signing, overlay data (e.g. an embedded game pack), toolchain/engine hints and strings. Read-only: it does not unpack, decrypt or patch.

strings.description: String options: min, limit, match, maxMB, raw.

maxMB.description: Scan this many MiB for strings (default 64).

raw.description: Include strings that look like byte noise (default false).

match.description: Filter import/export names: substring, glob or /regex/i.

limit.description: Import and export names to return each (default 100).

tools.name: re_archive
tools.description: Lists or extracts Godot .pck packs (also packs embedded in an exported .exe/.x86_64), ZIP family (apk, jar, ipa, nupkg, docx), tar and tar.gz (.unitypackage), and Electron .asar. Identifies Unity bundles and Unreal paks (header only). Godot entries are MD5-checked on extraction. Encrypted packs/entries are reported, never decrypted. Extraction goes to the ReversePort workspace unless out is given.

match.description: Only entries matching: substring, glob (*.gd, scenes/*.tscn) or /regex/.

tools.name: re_probe
tools.description: For unknown or custom formats: identifies the format at an offset, hex view, entropy map (text/code/compressed regions), embedded files (PNG, OGG, WAV, ZIP, GDPC, glTF, DDS, ELF/PE…) with offsets and sizes, and likely record strides for tables. Works on multi-GB files.

length.description: Bytes in the hex view (default 256, max 4096).

maxMB.description: MiB to scan for entropy/embedded files (default 512).

tools.name: re_extract
tools.description: Copies a byte range (e.g. an embedded PNG/WAV/glb/ZIP found by re_probe) into the workspace as its own file. length is optional when the embedded format stores its size (RIFF/WAV, glb, PNG). To unpack a whole archive or pack, use re_archive with action:"extract" instead.

tools.name: re_compare
tools.description: Compares two folders (added/removed/changed files), two packs/archives (entries, MD5 for Godot packs), two executables (imports, exports, sections) or any two files (first difference, changed regions). Use it to see what changed between builds or versions.

tools.name: re_report
tools.description: Writes ARCHITECTURE.md for a project: stack, languages, entry points, mermaid module graph, cycles, most-used files, scene trees of the entry scenes, class table, possibly unused files and external dependencies.

tools.name: re_lookup
tools.description: Recon without files: give one of query (a name), url (store/web/GitHub page), steamAppId, appStoreId or github. Reads public sources only (Steam store API, PCGamingWiki, Wikidata, Apple App Store, GitHub, the web page itself) and returns a dossier: identity (developer, release, platforms, genres), tech (engine with confidence and sources, languages, graphics APIs, middleware, web stack and hosting fingerprint), material (where its files live and how they are structured: install layout and formats of its engine, save/config locations, scripts/wasm/data files a web page loads, a public repo's structure and detected engine), references (screenshots, videos, pages), and open-source reimplementations, remakes and tools. mirror:true downloads a public GitHub repo's source text so re_graph, re_symbols and port_plan can read it. Returns a lookupId for re_blueprint. Cached for a day (fresh:true refetches).

query.description: Name of the game, app or software.

url.description: Steam, App Store, Google Play, GitHub or any public web page URL.

github.description: Public GitHub repo: owner/repo or URL.

sources.description: Limit sources (default all): steam, pcgamingwiki, wikidata, github, appstore, web.

mirror.description: GitHub: download the source text (code, scenes, configs) into the workspace.

tools.name: re_blueprint
tools.description: Turns a re_lookup dossier (lookupId) and/or name, genres, tags and a description into a clean-room rebuild spec that matches the original in function and feel: the systems it is made of, and per system the parameters to measure on the original (speeds, jump arcs, timings, frame data, camera, economy tables, UI layout fractions…) with how to measure them; target engine with conventions (same engine as the original by default); milestones; capture/measure/verify method; clean-room rules (own code, art, audio, text and name). Writes BLUEPRINT.md, parity.json (every parameter with original/rebuild/tolerance) and, for engine targets, a project skeleton with every numeric parameter as a tunable. Archetypes: platformer, shooter, racing, flight, rpg, roguelike, strategy, management, survival, puzzle, card, fighting, sports, narrative, multiplayer, idle, horror, social-app, productivity-app, shopping-app, media-app, fitness-app, web-saas.

name.description: Name of the original (when there is no lookupId).

kind.description: game or app (default from the lookup, else game).

description.description: What the original is and does.

engine.description: Engine of the original, if known.

target.description: Target: godot, godot-csharp, unity, unreal, threejs, or web, flutter, react-native, swift, kotlin, electron, or a language.

output.description: Project skeleton folder (new or empty; default workspace/blueprints/<name>/project-<target>).

scaffold.description: Write the project skeleton (default true for engine targets).

tools.name: port_map
tools.description: Curated porting knowledge: engine conventions (axes, units, handedness, Euler order, FOV, physics tick, lifecycle) and API maps with notes and pitfalls. Without arguments: lists engines and maps. Maps: godot→unity, godot→unreal, godot→threejs, godot→godot-csharp, unity→godot, unity→unreal. query/topic filter entries.

from.description: Source engine (godot, godot-csharp, unity, unreal, threejs).

topic.description: Exact topic (lifecycle, input, physics, events, scene tree, rendering…).

tools.name: port_convert
tools.description: Converts positions, rotations (quaternion [x,y,z,w] or Euler degrees in the source engine's convention), scales and camera FOV between godot, godot-csharp, threejs, gltf, bevy, unity, unity-xmirror, unreal, blender. Returns target quaternion plus Euler in the target's convention (Godot rotation_degrees, Unity eulerAngles, three.js), the axis matrix and unit factor (Unreal ×100).

euler.description: Euler degrees in the source convention (godot, unity, threejs).

fov.description: Camera FOV in degrees (vertical; horizontal for unreal).

tools.name: port_plan
tools.description: Plans a port of a project to another engine or language and creates the output project (scaffold). Every source file becomes a unit with a target path, action (translate, convert-scene, copy, rebuild), dependencies, API-usage count and risk, ordered dependencies-first. Engines: godot, godot-csharp, unity, unreal, threejs; or a language (typescript, python, csharp, cpp, rust, go…). The source is never modified; output must be a new or empty folder.

to.description: Target: godot, godot-csharp, unity, unreal, threejs or a language.

tools.name: port_unit
tools.description: Returns one unit with everything needed to port it: source text, symbols, the engine APIs it uses with their mapped equivalents and line numbers (apiHints), conventions, target path and naming rules, dependencies with the symbols of their already-ported targets, and a checklist. Marks it in_progress.

planId.description: Port plan id from port_plan (port_status lists them).

unit.description: Unit id (u001…), or its source/target path. Omit for the next unit in dependency order.

full.description: Repeat the conventions and checklist even after the first finished unit (they are shortened after that).

tools.name: port_write
tools.description: Writes the ported file(s) for a unit into the output project (never outside it) and records progress. Returns leftovers (source-engine APIs still present), PORT/TODO markers, source functions/signals missing in the port, and the next unit. copy:true copies an asset unchanged. Give exactly one of content, files or copy. status partial/skipped with notes when something cannot be ported yet.

planId.description: Port plan id from port_plan (port_status lists them).

content.description: File content for the unit target.

path.description: Path inside the output project (default: unit target).

notes.description: What is left or why it was skipped.

tools.name: port_scene
tools.description: Converts a scene deterministically: Godot .tscn → Unity prefab/scene spec (+ editor builder menu), three.js TypeScript builder module, Unreal scene spec (cm, Z-up) or Godot C# (script paths swapped); Unity .unity/.prefab → Godot .tscn (bodies, colliders, primitive meshes, cameras, lights, scripts, prefab instances). Transforms are converted between coordinate systems. With planId it writes the unit; with file+to it writes into the workspace.

planId.description: Port plan id from port_plan (port_status lists them).

unit.description: Unit id (u001…), or its source/target path. Omit for the next unit in dependency order.

tools.name: port_copy_assets
tools.description: Copies every pending asset unit (textures, audio, models, fonts, video) of a plan into the output project. match limits it with a regex.

planId.description: Port plan id from port_plan (port_status lists them).

tools.name: port_status
tools.description: Without planId: lists all port plans in the workspace with progress. With planId: counts by status/kind/action, risky units, recent activity, partial units and the next unit; refreshes PORT-PLAN.md in the output folder.

planId.description: Port plan id from port_plan (port_status lists them).

tools.name: port_verify
tools.description: Checks a port: missing output files, units not ported yet, source-engine API leftovers, functions and signals from the source that do not exist in the port (lifecycle renames understood), PORT/TODO markers, partial units. passed is true only when everything is ported and clean.

planId.description: Port plan id from port_plan (port_status lists them).

tools.name: share_feedback
tools.description: Optional, any time: note what worked, what was confusing or slow, and what would help next time. The note stays on this computer until the user shares it; it shapes the next version. It never changes your task.

tool.description: Tool the note is about (if any).

rating.description: How well it served the task, 1 (poorly) to 5 (very well).

friction.description: What got in the way: unclear text, wasted calls, too much output, errors without a next step…

agent.description: Who you are, if you like (client, model).

tools.name: set_tool_profile
tools.description: Switches how many tools are listed and how long their descriptions are: compact (small or older models, small context), standard (default), full (every engine tool). Nothing becomes unreachable: engine_tools and engine_call reach every tool in every profile. Clients that support list changes refresh automatically; others see it on the next tools/list.

tools.name: engine_tools
tools.description: Lists the deep-analysis engine tools that are not in your tool list (to keep it short), with a one-line summary each. query filters by words (e.g. "android class", "web network", "firmware"); names returns full input schemas. Call them with engine_call.

query.description: Words to look for in names and descriptions.

names.description: Tool names to show in full (with input schema).

tools.name: engine_call
tools.description: Calls a deep-analysis engine tool by name, including ones not in your tool list (find them with engine_tools). arguments follow that tool's input schema.

tools.name: procedure_callers
tools.description: Return the provider's resolved direct callers for one procedure identified by symbol or address. Results reflect completed static analysis and may omit unresolved indirect references.

document.description: The active target's provider document name; use open_binary to switch targets

tools.description: Decompile one analyzed procedure by symbol name or provider-normalized address. Returns provider-specific pseudocode, never original source or cross-provider text equivalence, and may return null; request procedure_assembly when instruction precision matters. Ghidra no-return assumptions may cut the analyzed body; Evidence limitations report observed terminal calls and available callee identities.

Results are deterministic and complete over those defined objects, not every text sequence in artifact bytes. Ghidra may omit packed or undefined literals, including Rust strings; an empty result does not prove text is absent. If an address is known, read_bytes and xrefs inspect its bytes and references. Hopper retains typed byte decoding, native display, and explicit decoding unknowns. Adjacent long-literal fragments match independently. Hopper regex mode uses ECMAScript Unicode syntax in a cancellable worker; a matching deadline leaves its API usable.

tools.name: analyze_function
tools.description: Build a dossier for one native function identified by symbol or provider-returned address. Returns identity with complete inclusive analyzed body ranges or explicit unknown, provider-specific pseudocode and assembly, comments, calls, references, referenced strings/names, local CFG blocks, and available native API boundary observations. Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut the analyzed body are reported in limitations with available callee identities.

tools.name: inspect_artifact
tools.description: Inspect an active archive or application package in one call. Returns the complete content-addressed artifact graph once, as the nested inventory Evidence, with root and integrity observations, integrity contradictions, hypotheses, unexplored branches, limitations, and next probes inline. Read-only DMG mounting is used automatically on supported macOS hosts. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue keeps mismatches explicitly untrusted. It does not extract files; use extract_artifact to materialize its regular contents.

tools.name: inspect_managed_artifact
tools.description: Open and classify an explicit managed PE/CLI path, or inspect the active managed target, then inventory exact assembly/module identity, target framework evidence, references, resources, and custom attributes without loading or executing target code. Returns complete inline inventories when metadata is admitted and explicit partial or malformed coverage otherwise.

tools.name: inspect_android_package
tools.description: Inspect a local APK's package, SDK and permission declarations, decoded manifest and class/resource counts. Does not execute the APK or verify signatures. Requires a caller-supplied JADX MCP JAR and JDK; uses one worker in an isolated temporary workspace.

tools.name: inspect_analysis_view
tools.description: Inspect selected views of completed binary-layout, JavaScript application or native analyze_function Evidence without repeating analysis. The api-surface view groups retained HAR requests by method, origin and format-rule path template; templated segments are inferences. It reads no headers or bodies and reports no query values. Use an exact same-session retained evidence_id or portable inline Evidence. Select a summary, layout mitigations/linkage facet, one section/symbol/module, or a stable page. Module pages include assets, bundled and source modules; use node_id for ambiguous or unavailable paths. Native views select procedure, pseudocode, assembly, basic blocks, comments, callers/callees, references, unresolved calls, referenced strings/names, native API and high-pcode. Use nonnegative offset and a positive caller-selected limit (defaults 0 and 64); pseudocode uses UTF-16 code units, other native pages use rows. Returns artifact identity, parent Evidence ID, a distinct view digest, coverage, limitations and unknowns. Actual serialized size determines MCP transport admission; choose a smaller page or export the complete retained Evidence if needed.

tools.name: analyze_javascript_application
tools.description: Reconstruct one local ASAR or extracted JavaScript application as an inline application graph without executing it. Returns recovered graph nodes, edges, semantic relations, integrity contradictions, limitations, and coverage. Select source_paths to acquire and analyze only exact inventoried file paths; the complete artifact inventory and identity remain intact, and unselected sources remain explicit unknowns. Dependencies are not implicitly analyzed. Select detail summary to retain the complete analysis Evidence in this session and receive only its summary view, then inspect selected modules or pages with inspect_analysis_view. Summary detail reduces delivery, whereas source_paths bounds source analysis. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue retains observed bytes as untrusted and marks graph coverage partial.

tools.description: Open a local executable, application bundle, archive, JavaScript, source map, plist, or analysis database after validation. format=dos-com explicitly interprets 1..65280 headerless bytes as a DOS COM analysis image. format=raw-binary interprets headerless bytes with a required architecture and entry_point; file offset 0 maps at that address. instructions:
ReversePort: reverse engineer anything, port it anywhere. It runs on this machine, never modifies the targets it reads, and writes output to new folders. re_lookup reads public web pages; runtime-observation tools run only the target you name.
Projects and exported games: re_scan {path} (engine, version, entry points) → re_graph → re_symbols / re_scene; re_report writes ARCHITECTURE.md.
Files at a glance: re_binary (executables), re_archive (Godot .pck also inside an .exe, zip/apk/jar, asar; action:"extract" to unpack), re_probe (unknown data), re_compare (two builds).
Compiled code in depth (engine): open_binary → search_procedures / search_strings → analyze_function or procedure_pseudo_code, xrefs, procedure_callers → close_binary. .NET: inspect_managed_artifact. Android code: inspect_android_package. Electron/JS: analyze_javascript_application. Open browser page: list_browser_targets. Large engine results: pass detail:"summary" and page with inspect_analysis_view. If an engine tool refuses, binary_session {} says why and how to fix it. More engine tools (also ones engine prompts mention): engine_tools {query} to find, engine_call {tool, arguments} to use.
No files: re_lookup {query|url|github} → re_blueprint (clean-room rebuild spec with parameters to measure). Port: port_map → port_plan → port_unit → write the code → port_write (scenes: port_scene) → port_verify; the loop is built so any model can do it one unit at a time — leave PORT: markers rather than guess. Results with an obvious next step carry next/nextCall with the exact call. Use port_convert for every transform.
Work at your own pace: start with summaries, narrow with match/limit, and stop to ask the user when the target or scope is unclear — a partial answer with its gaps named is better than a guess. Short on context? set_tool_profile {profile:"compact"}; want everything listed? "full". If something here gets in your way, share_feedback tells the maintainers.
